title: Headwaters
tagline: 2,371 datasets worth working with, and the 54 sources they come from — classified, searchable, probed.
blurb: Two catalogues in one. The dataset layer holds 2,371 published datasets drawn from two aggregations that select for very different things - every TidyTuesday week since April 2018, which is tidy and teachable and comes with 8,575 column names, and ten years of Data Is Plural, which is odd and specific and global. Each record carries the curator's own pitch, the upstream publisher and the article that prompted it, classified by subject, publisher and place so you can browse for something to work with rather than search for something you already know exists; the 30 datasets both aggregations surfaced are one record with two sightings, and a facet filters on how a dataset was found. The source layer holds 54 endpoints you can query repeatedly, each described well enough to use from a shell and carrying small real requests that a weekly job re-runs to prove the endpoint still works. Building it turned up failures nothing else documents, including data.gov's CKAN API 404ing on every documented path while its gateway authenticates your key and redirects you to the dead origin, SEC EDGAR refusing any User-Agent that contains the string github.com while accepting the same header with any other domain, and ProPublica's Congress API being retired outright while its documentation site still serves 200.
